title: Lamin B1-dependent regulation of human separase in mitosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the complete Europe PMC supplementary package (8.5 MB): it holds 16 figure images (GIF/WEBP of the main-text figures) plus one 19-page PDF. I extracted the text of all 19 PDF pages with pypdf: pages 1-7 are supplementary figure legends and extra methods, pages 8-19 are image panels with only a caption line of text. There is no spreadsheet, CSV, TSV or any numeric table anywhere in the package. I also searched the full open-access text (95,825 characters) for deposition keywords: zero hits for mass spectrometry, proteomics, PRIDE, BioImage Archive, Zenodo, figshare, RNA-seq, GSE or 'deposited'.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement, which reads in full: 'All data supporting this study are available within the main figures and supplementary data file.' Also from the text only: the assay descriptions (immunofluorescence, proximity ligation assay, Western blot, flow-cytometry cell-cycle profiling, time-lapse microscopy of a separase activity sensor in HeLa cells) and the fact that most quantifications come from 2-6 independent experiments.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset to download. The only files attached to the paper are figure images and a 19-page PDF of supplementary figures and legends, which I opened and read. No repository accession exists (no GEO, SRA, PRIDE, BioImage Archive, Zenodo or Dryad record found by the automated accession scan or by my own keyword search of the full text). The underlying microscopy images and per-cell measurements were never deposited.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No column exists anywhere, because no table exists. Every quantity in this paper (separase fluorescence intensity on chromosomes, proximity ligation assay dots per nucleus, percentage of cells with premature chromatid separation, centrosome counts) lives only as a plotted bar or dot in a figure image. Building a label would mean digitising pixels out of PDF charts.

a3_inputs_present.note: No model inputs are present either: the raw microscopy images are not shared, and the only sequences involved are two human proteins (separase/ESPL1 and lamin B1), so there is nothing to featurise.

a4_units_stated.note: Where numbers appear in figure legends they do carry units or clear normalisation (kDa for blots, 'PLA dots per nucleus', '% of cells', fluorescence intensity in arbitrary units). This is the one Part A item that does not fail, but it is moot given A1.

a5_enough_rows.note: No row count can be given because no table exists. The experimental unit is the individual cell scored by microscopy across 2-6 independent experiments; legends say 'the number of analyzed cells for each condition is indicated below each bar', i.e. counts are printed inside figure images only. Even if digitised, this is a handful of conditions, far under the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but small because it contains no data.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper's claims.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle: every measurement traces to a physical assay (antibody staining, proximity ligation, blotting, flow cytometry), nothing is another model's output. Irrelevant, since the measurements are not released.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no measurements, only pictures of measurements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use mitotic cell images to predict whether sister chromosomes separate too early when a nuclear envelope protein is disturbed.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on single-cell microscopy images of dividing human fibroblasts, labelled by how much lamin B1 (a nuclear envelope scaffold protein) each cell has. The number of such cells is unknown: counts are printed inside figure images and the images themselves were never shared.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be a per-cell call of premature chromatid separation or diplochromosome formation, scored by a cytogeneticist eyeballing metaphase chromosome spreads down a microscope.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Scoring chromosome-separation defects by eye is slow, subjective lab work, so an automated scorer would help cell-cycle and genome-instability labs. None of that is testable here because the images are not released.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The only conceivable task, automated scoring of chromosome-separation defects from mitotic cell images, needs the raw microscopy that this paper does not share. If someone wanted that project, the data would have to come from an image repository such as the BioImage Archive or the Image Data Resource, not from here.

effort.compute_note: Only the 8.5 MB supplementary package exists; I downloaded and parsed it in seconds. No modelling estimate is meaningful because there is no data to model.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the supplementary package and look for a single spreadsheet. There is none; it is 16 figure images plus a 19-page PDF of legends and panels. That took one command and killed the project.

verdict_reason: A pure wet-lab cell-biology paper with nothing deposited. The data availability statement says all data are 'within the main figures and supplementary data file', and I confirmed by opening that file: 16 figure images and a 19-page PDF of legends, methods and image panels, with zero tables. Part A1 (no downloadable data), A2 (no label column; it would have to be read off bar charts), A3, A5 and A7 all fail. Stopped at the first killer, so Parts B-J were not scored.
